task.prompt: verify that you are able to identify task.
task.requirements: this task was marked as in progress, and xml was saved
task.notes: Task identified by id ZP-3. Marked in-progress and saved tasks.xml, then completed and saved again.

task.prompt: add a mouse over tool tip that shows notes from the agent, any error codes from the agent if posted, and the files changed if complete
task.requirements: the tooltil is implement and successfully shows
task.notes: Added a ToolTip to every task row in MainWindow.xaml. It shows an Error section (when errorMessage is set), a Notes section (when notes are set) and a Files changed section (when filesChanged is set); each section is hidden when its field is empty, with a fallback line when nothing is recorded. Added AllEmptyToVisibilityConverter (IMultiValueConverter) to support the fallback. Also added Error/ErrorMessage/Commit/Build/Release to the TaskItem model and to TaskXmlSerializer so the tooltip has data to bind to.

task.prompt: add an error tag to the xml, and a space for error messages to be posted
task.requirements: the tag and error message xml tag exists
task.notes: The <error> boolean tag and the <errorMessage> text tag are now written and read for every task by TaskXmlSerializer, and are present on every task in this file. Backed by TaskItem.Error / TaskItem.ErrorMessage. ParseBool defaults <error> to false when the element is absent, so older files still load.

task.prompt: add displays to the pop up editor for errors, error messages, notes from the agent, and files changed ONLY if these files are populated
task.requirements: the files show up when they are populated
task.notes: The task edit pop-up now shows an Error section (error flag + error message), a Notes section, and a Files changed section, each rendered ONLY when that field was already populated when the pop-up opened. Visibility is latched in TaskFormViewModel (HasError / HasNotes / HasFilesChanged) so editing the text does not make a section disappear. Replaced the old ShowAgentFields gate.

task.prompt: add an error message to this task and add notes that say "error message posed" in the error message field
task.notes: error message posed. This error was posted deliberately per the ZP-7 prompt to exercise the error-display path (row tooltip, pop-up editor Error section, and the red row background added by ZP-9). The task requirement "the error was posted" is met, so execution continues to the next task rather than halting (the halt rule applies only to tasks that are impossible to complete).

task.prompt: change it so pressing tab moves from prompt to requirements instead in inserting a tab, make shift tab work also
task.requirements: tab and shift tab works as well
task.notes: Set AcceptsTab="False" on the Prompt and Requirements text boxes in the task pop-up (overriding the EditorTextBox style, which keeps AcceptsTab for the full-page design/instruction editor). Tab now moves focus Prompt -> Requirements -> the In progress / Done checkboxes, and Shift+Tab moves backwards, using WPF's standard focus traversal.

task.prompt: give error tasks a red background
task.notes: Task rows now use a Style with a DataTrigger on Error=True that swaps the row background to a restrained low-saturation red (ErrorSurfaceBrush #FBEAEA) and the border to ErrorBorderBrush. Added ErrorSurface/ErrorBorder/ErrorText brushes to Theme/Styles.xaml. ZP-7 is flagged as an error and now renders red.

task.prompt: add commit checkbox to top right of pop-up text editor and tag to xml, to indicate we should push to github
task.notes: Added a "Commit" checkbox to the top-right of the task pop-up (header restructured into a Grid: title/ID on the left, checkbox row on the right). Bound to TaskFormViewModel.Commit -> TaskItem.Commit. The <commit> XML tag is written and read by TaskXmlSerializer and is present on every task in this file. Per instructions.txt, a task with commit=true triggers a project commit + push once it is done.

task.prompt: rather than up and down arrows, use click and drag to reorder tasks.
task.requirements: tasks can now be reordered by clicking and draggin
task.notes: Removed the up/down arrow buttons from each task row and the ORDER column. Reordering is now click-and-drag: press on a row and drag it onto another row to drop it there (handled by TaskItem_PreviewMouseLeftButtonDown / MouseMove / Drop in MainWindow.xaml.cs via DragDrop.DoDragDrop; MainViewModel.MoveTask persists the new order and normalizes). Added a grip glyph and "drag to reorder" affordance in the first column and header. Removed the now-unused MoveTaskUp/Down commands and MoveTaskBy from MainViewModel.

task.prompt: add build checkbox, indicating the project should be built once this task is done
task.notes: Added a "Build" checkbox next to "Commit" in the task pop-up top-right, bound to TaskFormViewModel.Build -> TaskItem.Build. The <build> XML tag is written/read by TaskXmlSerializer and present on every task. Per instructions.txt, build=true means the project is built to builds/debug once the task is done (builds/test for test builds, builds/release when release is also set).

task.prompt: add a release check box next ot build and commit checkboxes indicating a release build should be made
task.notes: Added a "Release" checkbox next to Commit and Build in the task pop-up top-right, bound to TaskFormViewModel.Release -> TaskItem.Release. The <release> XML tag is written/read by TaskXmlSerializer and present on every task. Per instructions.txt, release=true means a release build is produced to builds/release once the task is done.

task.prompt: add a small preview when your dragging tasks around (while you are still holding the task, physically move the box with the mouse. when it comes in between two other tasks, move the bottom task down to make room, when it moves out of that gap, close the gap again.)
task.requirements: task moving is more visually acceptable
task.notes: Replaced OLE drag-and-drop with a manual drag. On drag start the row is snapshotted to a RenderTargetBitmap and shown as a semi-transparent "ghost" (RowDragAdorner) that follows the mouse; the real row is collapsed so the list closes up behind it. As the pointer passes each row's midpoint an insertion index is computed and every row at/after it animates down by the row height (120ms CubicEase) to open a gap; moving away animates the gap closed. On mouse-up the task is moved to that index via MainViewModel.MoveTaskToIndex and the order is persisted. ListBox switched to a non-virtualizing StackPanel items host so container transforms are stable. Built to builds/debug and committed per the commit/build flags.

task.prompt: all complete tasks, appear at the bottom of the list and there is a button to collapse the complete list. there is a clear divider between active and complete tasks.
task.requirements: tasks are now sorted by completion
task.notes: The task list is now grouped into sections via a grouped ICollectionView (MainViewModel.TasksView) with a PropertyGroupDescription on TaskItem.SectionKey. Project.Tasks is kept physically stable-sorted by SectionRank (SortIntoSections, called from AfterTasksChanged on every add/edit/toggle/reorder) so drag-reorder stays index-based. Sections render in order: "Needs attention", "Active", "Completed". Each section has a clear divider (thin rule + small caps label + count) from a GroupStyle.ContainerStyle template. The "Completed" section (all done tasks, at the bottom) has a Show/Hide button that toggles MainViewModel.CompletedCollapsed; a MultiDataTrigger collapses that group's ItemsPresenter when set. Verified visually.

task.prompt: tasks with an error that are not complete are at the top of the list, this divider is clear
task.requirements: error tasks are at the top of the list
task.notes: Unfinished error tasks (TaskItem.SectionRank 0) already sort to the top as the "Needs attention" group from ZP-16. Made that divider unmistakable: the section header bar gets a pale-red background (ErrorSurfaceBrush), a red top/bottom rule (ErrorBorderBrush, 2px top / 1px bottom) and red small-caps label text, via DataTriggers on the group name in the GroupItem template. Confirmed in the grouped-list screenshot: "Needs attention (1)" sits above "Active" and "Completed".

task.prompt: save an active database of projects and tasks to the executable direcory as data.cfg this contains all projects and paths as well as copies of the global design instructions and prompt that then just get copied
task.notes: Workspace now writes data.cfg next to the executable (AppContext.BaseDirectory) on load and on every Save(). It is an XML "promptQueueData" database holding every project (name + directory path + its full task queue via TaskXmlSerializer.ToElement) plus verbatim CDATA copies of the global design / instructions / prompt. If the executable directory is read-only the write is skipped silently. On startup, when there is no per-user workspace.xml, the workspace hydrates projects + globals from data.cfg instead. New projects with no local design/instructions/prompt are now seeded with copies of the globals ("that then just get copied"). Built to builds/debug and builds/release and committed per the build/release/commit flags.

task.prompt: design, generate, and use a icon for this project that is inline with the design astetic
task.notes: Designed a restrained checklist mark in the app's own palette (off-white rounded tile with a thin #C7C7C7 border, charcoal #282828 marks, one muted-blue #4B6EA8 accent checkbox with a white tick, three task bars of decreasing weight). Generated a real multi-resolution icon (16/24/32/48/64/128/256, PNG-compressed frames) at src/PromptQueue.App/Assets/app.ico via a System.Drawing generator script. Wired it up: <ApplicationIcon> in the csproj (shell / taskbar / exe) and Window.Icon="pack://application:,,,/Assets/app.ico" (title bar). Verified the icon shows in the title bar and taskbar.

task.prompt: when the project is closed it goes to the task bar, when it is restored it automatically reloads all projects
task.notes: Pressing the window's close [X] now cancels the close and minimises to the taskbar instead (MainWindow.OnClosing). Restoring from minimised (MainWindow.OnStateChanged, _wasMinimized latch) calls MainViewModel.ReloadAllProjects(), which re-reads tasks.xml and the local design/instructions/prompt for every known project via the new ProjectStore.ReloadInto and rebuilds the grouped view. Real quit is still available via File > Exit, which raises MainViewModel.ExitRequested; the window sets an _allowClose flag and closes for real.

task.prompt: change the application name to zProject
task.requirements: project name and exe name changed
task.notes: Renamed the application to "zProject": csproj now sets AssemblyName/Product/AssemblyTitle=zProject so the build output is zProject.exe; the window Title is "zProject"; the two MessageBox captions (delete-task confirm, unhandled-exception) say "zProject". Verified: title bar and taskbar show "zProject" with the new icon, and builds/*/zProject.exe is produced. Built to builds/debug and builds/release and committed per the flags.

task.prompt: add support for subtasks, when creating a task subtasks can be designed. create a simple ui where each one is a small line, each subtask can be checked off one by one.
task.notes: New Subtask model (Text + Done) and TaskItem.Subtasks (ObservableCollection). Serialized inside <task> as <subtasks><subtask done="false">text</subtask>...</subtasks> (read + write); flows into data.cfg too. The Add/Edit task pop-up has a Subtasks section: each existing subtask is one line (checkbox + editable text + remove button) and a "new subtask" box (Enter or Add). Each task row shows a "checkbox n/m" progress badge and an inline checklist whose checkboxes toggle Subtask.Done and persist immediately; the tooltip also lists them. TaskItem re-raises SubtaskProgress when a subtask's Done changes. Verified: SD-1 shows "2/4" and its checklist renders.

task.prompt: add a new checkbox for "bugs" to be identified as bugs, these are automatically at the TOP of the xml file when saving no matter where it is in the list
task.notes: Added a "Bug" checkbox to the task pop-up (next to In progress / Done), bound to TaskFormViewModel.Bug -> TaskItem.Bug. New <bug> tag read/written by TaskXmlSerializer. When serializing, tasks are ordered OrderByDescending(Bug).ThenBy(Order), so every bug is written at the TOP of tasks.xml regardless of its position in the list. In the app, an unfinished bug also sorts into a top "Bugs" section (TaskItem.SectionRank 0) ahead of "Needs attention" / "Active" / "Completed".

task.prompt:
more color-coding red: errors purple: bugs green: done
all colors should be kind of pale and washed out
task.notes: Added pale, washed-out Bug (purple #F1ECF8) and Done (green #EAF3EC) surface/border/text brushes alongside the existing pale Error red, in Theme/Styles.xaml. Task rows now colour-code via Style triggers: done -> green, unfinished error -> red, unfinished bug -> purple (bug wins over error). Section dividers match: "Bugs" purple, "Needs attention" red, "Completed" green.

task.prompt: add displays from the main view for bug,error,commit,build,and release so i can see at a glance
task.notes: Each task row now shows a compact row of status chips (new StatusChip / StatusChipText styles) directly under the prompt/requirements: BUG (purple), ERROR (red), COMMIT, BUILD (neutral) and RELEASE (accent). Each chip is shown only when its flag is set; the whole strip is hidden when none are, via an AllEmpty MultiBinding. Verified the sections + row tints render (Bugs / Needs attention / Active / Completed).

task.prompt: right next to add task, add a text field for comma seperated tags, keep track (per project) of each tag and autocomplete exisiting ones as they are typed. color code each tag a random color, again this is for easy identification, these tags will also be saved to the xml (text only) so the agent cant tell what it is
task.notes: Tasks carry TaskItem.TagText (comma-separated, stored verbatim in a <tags> xml element so it is opaque to an agent) and a parsed Tags list. Next to "Add Task" there is an editable, text-search ComboBox whose dropdown is the project's KnownTags (every distinct tag in the project, recomputed on any change) — typing autocompletes existing tags; its value pre-fills the Tags field of the next new task. The edit pop-up has a "Tags (comma separated)" field with a live preview of colour chips. Each tag renders as a chip whose colour is derived deterministically from the tag text (FNV hash -> hue -> pale HSL) via TagColorConverter, so the same tag is always the same washed-out colour for easy identification, on both the row and the pop-up. Built to builds/debug and builds/release and committed.

task.prompt: add save current to only save the open project
task.notes: Added "File > Save Current Project" (MainViewModel.SaveCurrentCommand -> SaveCurrentProject). It writes only the selected project's files (tasks.xml + local design/instructions/prompt via ProjectStore.Save) and refreshes data.cfg, without touching any other project — unlike "Save All".

task.prompt: add a lock icon to all tasks, if unlock the icon looks like an unlocked padlock and the AI uses the task, if locked the padlock becomes locked, the task backgorund becomes grey, and the ai ignores the task due to a tag in the xml indicating the locked task.
task.notes: Every task row has a padlock toggle button (Segoe MDL2 Assets glyphs — open padlock when unlocked, closed padlock when locked) via LockGlyphConverter and MainViewModel.ToggleTaskLockCommand. Locking sets TaskItem.Locked, serialized as the <locked> xml tag, and a DataTrigger greys the whole card (LockedSurfaceBrush #E6E6E6, wins over all colour-coding). The task pop-up also has a Locked checkbox. instructions.txt now has a SKIP RULES section telling an agent to skip any task with <locked>true</locked>. All four subtasks complete.

task.prompt: add a blocked by field, that containes an (autocomplete) task ID (and also show the name if available) if an AI hits a blocked task, it completes the blocked by task first, if it cant then it skips them both. show blocked by ID on task preview card
task.notes: TaskItem.BlockedBy (task id) with the <blockedBy> xml tag. The pop-up has an editable, text-search "Blocked by" ComboBox whose candidates are the project's other tasks shown as "ID — name"; on save the leading id is extracted. The app resolves the blocker's name (MainViewModel.ResolveBlockedByNames) into TaskItem.BlockedByLabel, and the preview card shows "⛔ blocked by ID — name" when set. instructions.txt SKIP RULES: an agent completes the blocker first, and if it cannot (blocker locked/archived/missing/impossible) it skips both.

task.prompt: add due date and date started field, as well as time due, use a calendar picker and display the time correctly formatted.
task.notes: TaskItem.DateStarted and TaskItem.DueDate (nullable DateTime). The pop-up has a WPF DatePicker calendar picker for each, with a small "HH:mm" time box beside it; TaskFormViewModel splits/recombines the date and time parts. Serialized as <dateStarted> / <dueDate> in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" (invariant, 24h). The preview card shows a formatted "Started 2026-09-01 09:30 • Due 2026-09-05 17:00" line (TaskItem.DatesSummary) when either is set. Built to builds/debug and builds/release and committed.

task.prompt: make preview cards collapsable, show only name, status, and ID as well as colorcoding
task.notes: Every card has a chevron toggle (ChevronGlyphConverter, Segoe MDL2) bound to a runtime-only TaskItem.Collapsed via MainViewModel.ToggleTaskCollapsedCommand. Collapsed cards show only: the name (TaskItem.DisplayName), the single-word status (TaskItem.StatusText), the ID, and the colour-coded background/border (which still applies). The detail block (prompt/requirements/blocked-by/dates/chips/subtasks) is hidden via a Visibility bound to Expanded. Tags are separately collapsable on an expanded card via a small ToggleButton bound to TaskItem.TagsCollapsed (new ToolbarToggle style). All five subtasks complete.

task.prompt: add optional name field to cards, if blank assume the ID for the name
task.notes: TaskItem.Name (optional) with the <name> xml tag; TaskItem.DisplayName returns Name when set, otherwise the Id. The task pop-up has a "Name (optional — defaults to the ID)" field at the top. Cards show DisplayName as the primary label, with the Id shown as a small secondary line only when a distinct Name is set (TaskItem.HasName). The Blocked-by autocomplete and its card label also use "ID — name".

task.prompt: ensure reload button only reloads the currently opened project
task.notes: Verified and tightened: the Reload button and "File > Reload Project from Disk" both call MainViewModel.ReloadProject, which re-reads ONLY SelectedProject via ProjectStore.ReloadInto (tasks.xml + local design/instructions/prompt) and rebuilds just that project's grouped view; no other open project is read or written. Status now reads "Reloaded only \"X\" from disk". (Reloading every project is a separate path, ReloadAllProjects, used only on window-restore per ZP-20.) Built to builds/debug; the Release build is deferred because an app instance is currently running from builds/release — Release config compiles clean and will be emitted there once it is closed.

task.prompt: move all cards marked done to a new tag called "archived" archived tasks still show in this app, but AI will ignore them completly
task.notes: TaskItem.Archived + <archived> xml tag (kept as a dedicated flag, like <locked>, rather than a visible text tag so it actually signals an agent). New "Archive done" button in the project header runs MainViewModel.ArchiveDoneCommand, which sets Archived on every done, not-yet-archived task. Archived tasks still show in the app in their own bottom "Archived" section (SectionRank 4) with a grey divider and grey card background. instructions.txt SKIP RULES: an agent skips any <archived>true</archived> task entirely.

task.prompt: if a card is blocked by another, position it automatically direcrtly under that card and slightly indented, if unblocked undo this, in the xml keep its original position, and move it back to that position when finished
task.notes: Blocked cards are repositioned in the list view only — the xml Order is never touched, so an unblocked card snaps straight back to its real position. MainViewModel.RecomputeBlockedLayout gives each task a runtime DisplayOrder (= Order, but nudged to blocker.DisplayOrder + tiny epsilon when blocked, a few passes for short chains) and an IndentLevel (blocker.IndentLevel + 1). The grouped ListCollectionView uses a CustomSort by (SectionRank, DisplayOrder), and the card's left Margin is bound to IndentLevel via IndentConverter (18px per level). Verified: "Wire the API" (blocked by BK-1) sits directly under "Set up database", indented. Built to builds/debug; Release build deferred while an app instance runs from builds/release.

task.prompt: build out webserver , it should be view only for the tasks for all project, you cannot edit tasks from the webview. while the server is running it opens a new console window with info.
task.notes: New console project src/PromptQueue.Server (AssemblyName zProject_server) built on HttpListener, referencing PromptQueue.Core so it reads the exact same workspace/tasks.xml as the app. It is strictly read-only — no write endpoints. Single-page zProject_webView.html: a project picker (all projects with open/done/total counts) and a per-project task view that mirrors the app's rules (Bugs/Needs attention/Active/Completed/Archived sections, pale colour-coding, BUG/ERROR/COMMIT/BUILD/RELEASE + deterministic tag chips, collapsible cards, subtask checklist, blocked-by line, locked/archived greying). Console: prints a banner with the address+port, logs every request with client IP and timing, logs SSE client connect/disconnect with an active count, and every 120s (and on each client connect) re-reads all projects from disk and pushes a "reload" event so open pages refresh; the page also polls every 120s as a fallback. Each /api/project/{i} call re-reads that project's tasks.xml, so switching projects always shows fresh data. The app's new "Server > Start Web View Server" menu launches zProject_server.exe (a console app, so it opens its own window). A build now means building BOTH projects into the same folder (documented in instructions.txt); zProject.exe, zProject_server.exe and zProject_webView.html are co-located in builds/test, builds/debug and builds/release. Verified end to end: picker + task view render correctly (headless screenshots), API returns all projects/tasks, console logs address/requests/connect/disconnect.
